```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

out_dir="/Volumes/Informatics/AlisePonsero/Krishani_CompassMe/VERVE_test"
sample_sheet="/Volumes/Informatics/AlisePonsero/Krishani_CompassMe/samples.tsv"
```

# Thresholds

Edit this chunk to change the flags. Nothing is ever excluded: these produce
warnings only, and every sample stays in the outputs regardless of its flags.

`direction` says which side is bad: `low` means small values are a problem
(depth, genes detected), `high` means large values are (rRNA, duplication).
Set a threshold to `NA` to switch that level off.

```{r thresholds}
thresholds <- tribble(
  ~metric,              ~label,                    ~direction, ~warn,  ~fail,
  "assigned_fragments", "Assigned fragments",      "low",      5e6,    1e6,
  "genes_detected_10",  "Genes detected (10+)",    "low",      10000,  5000,
  "median_cv_coverage", "Median CV coverage",      "high",     0.8,    1.0,
  "rrna_pct",           "rRNA (SortMeRNA)",        "high",     50,     75,
  "duplication_pct",    "Duplication",             "high",     80,     NA,
  "intergenic_pct",     "Intergenic bases",        "high",     50,     70,
  "correct_strand_pct", "Correct strand",          "low",      95,     90,
  "unique_map_pct",     "Uniquely mapped",         "low",      30,     15
)

# Requirements for locus-level ERV quantification. If any is not met, the
# sample is reported as suitable for family-level aggregation only.
locus_level_rules <- list(
  assigned_fragments = 5e6,
  genes_detected_10  = 10000,
  median_cv_coverage = 0.8   # upper limit
)

# Minimum count for a gene to be called detected
gene_detect_min <- 10
```

```{r paths}
out_step   <- file.path(out_dir, "01_host")
dir_align  <- file.path(out_step, "align")
dir_bamqc  <- file.path(out_step, "bamqc")
dir_rrna   <- file.path(out_step, "rrna")
dir_counts <- file.path(out_step, "counts")

samples_meta <- read_tsv(sample_sheet, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  select(any_of(c("sample_id", "body_site", "group", "batch")))

sample_ids <- samples_meta$sample_id
```

```{r parsers}
# STAR Log.final.out -----------------------------------------------------------
parse_star <- function(sample_id) {
  f <- file.path(dir_align, paste0(sample_id, ".Log.final.out"))
  if (!file.exists(f)) return(tibble(sample_id = sample_id))
  lines <- read_lines(f)
  grab <- function(pattern) {
    hit <- str_subset(lines, fixed(pattern))
    if (length(hit) == 0) return(NA_real_)
    hit[1] |> str_split("\\|") |> pluck(1, 2) |> str_remove("%") |>
      str_trim() |> as.numeric()
  }
  tibble(
    sample_id       = sample_id,
    input_reads     = grab("Number of input reads"),
    unique_map_pct  = grab("Uniquely mapped reads %"),
    multi_map_pct   = grab("% of reads mapped to multiple loci"),
    too_many_pct    = grab("% of reads mapped to too many loci"),
    unmapped_short_pct = grab("% of reads unmapped: too short")
  )
}

# Picard metrics files ---------------------------------------------------------
# One "## METRICS CLASS" block: header line, then one data row per read group
# or library (the first row is used).
parse_picard <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(tibble())
  lines <- read_lines(path)
  start <- str_which(lines, "^## METRICS CLASS")
  if (length(start) == 0) return(tibble())
  header <- str_split(lines[start + 1], "\t")[[1]]
  values <- str_split(lines[start + 2], "\t")[[1]]
  length(values) <- length(header)
  set_names(as.list(values), header) |> as_tibble()
}

# Fetch the first field present among the names given, as a single number.
# Returns NA if the file does not carry any of them, so a Picard version that
# renames a field degrades to a missing value rather than an error.
pick_num <- function(m, ...) {
  nm <- intersect(c(...), names(m))
  if (length(nm) == 0 || nrow(m) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  suppressWarnings(as.numeric(m[[nm[1]]][1]))
}

parse_rnaseq_metrics <- function(sample_id) {
  m <- parse_picard(file.path(dir_bamqc, paste0(sample_id, ".rnaseq_metrics.txt")))
  tibble(
    sample_id          = sample_id,
    coding_pct         = 100 * pick_num(m, "PCT_CODING_BASES", "PCT_CODING"),
    utr_pct            = 100 * pick_num(m, "PCT_UTR_BASES", "PCT_UTR"),
    intronic_pct       = 100 * pick_num(m, "PCT_INTRONIC_BASES", "PCT_INTRONIC"),
    intergenic_pct     = 100 * pick_num(m, "PCT_INTERGENIC_BASES", "PCT_INTERGENIC"),
    mrna_pct           = 100 * pick_num(m, "PCT_MRNA_BASES"),
    correct_strand_pct = 100 * pick_num(m, "PCT_CORRECT_STRAND_READS"),
    median_cv_coverage = pick_num(m, "MEDIAN_CV_COVERAGE"),
    bias_5p_to_3p      = pick_num(m, "MEDIAN_5PRIME_TO_3PRIME_BIAS")
  )
}

parse_markdup <- function(sample_id) {
  m <- parse_picard(file.path(dir_bamqc, paste0(sample_id, ".markdup_metrics.txt")))
  tibble(
    sample_id       = sample_id,
    duplication_pct = 100 * pick_num(m, "PERCENT_DUPLICATION")
  )
}

# SortMeRNA log ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Tolerant parsing: the total and the aligned count are read by pattern, and
# NA is returned if the log format does not match, rather than guessing.
parse_sortmerna <- function(sample_id) {
  f <- file.path(dir_rrna, paste0(sample_id, ".log"))
  if (!file.exists(f)) return(tibble(sample_id = sample_id))
  lines <- read_lines(f)
  num_after <- function(pattern) {
    hit <- str_subset(lines, regex(pattern, ignore_case = TRUE))
    if (length(hit) == 0) return(NA_real_)
    str_extract(hit[1], "[0-9]+(?=\\s*(\\(|$))|[0-9]+") |> as.numeric()
  }
  total   <- num_after("Total reads\\s*=")
  aligned <- num_after("Total reads passing E-value threshold")
  tibble(
    sample_id     = sample_id,
    rrna_reads    = aligned,
    rrna_total    = total,
    rrna_pct      = if (is.na(aligned) || is.na(total) || total == 0) NA_real_
                    else 100 * aligned / total
  )
}
```

```{r counts}
# featureCounts summary --------------------------------------------------------
summary_file <- file.path(dir_counts, "gene_counts.txt.summary")
fc_summary <- read_tsv(summary_file, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  rename(status = 1) |>
  pivot_longer(-status, names_to = "bam", values_to = "n") |>
  mutate(sample_id = basename(bam) |> str_remove("\\.markdup\\.bam$")) |>
  group_by(sample_id) |>
  summarise(
    assigned_fragments = n[status == "Assigned"],
    assigned_pct       = 100 * n[status == "Assigned"] / sum(n),
    multimapping_pct   = 100 * n[status == "Unassigned_MultiMapping"] / sum(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Gene count matrix ------------------------------------------------------------
counts_file <- file.path(dir_counts, "gene_counts.txt")
counts <- read_tsv(counts_file, comment = "#", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  select(Geneid, ends_with(".bam")) |>
  rename_with(~ basename(.x) |> str_remove("\\.markdup\\.bam$"), ends_with(".bam"))

genes_detected <- counts |>
  pivot_longer(-Geneid, names_to = "sample_id", values_to = "count") |>
  group_by(sample_id) |>
  summarise(genes_detected_10 = sum(count >= gene_detect_min), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r assemble}
metrics <- samples_meta |>
  left_join(map_dfr(sample_ids, parse_star), by = "sample_id") |>
  left_join(map_dfr(sample_ids, parse_rnaseq_metrics), by = "sample_id") |>
  left_join(map_dfr(sample_ids, parse_markdup), by = "sample_id") |>
  left_join(map_dfr(sample_ids, parse_sortmerna), by = "sample_id") |>
  left_join(fc_summary, by = "sample_id") |>
  left_join(genes_detected, by = "sample_id")

is_blank <- function(x) !is.na(x) & str_starts(x, "blank")
```

# Run summary

Input reads are STAR input fragments (read pairs). Assigned fragments are
featureCounts fragments in genes. rRNA is the SortMeRNA fraction over all
reads, not the Picard ribosomal metric (see notes).

```{r summary_table}
metrics |>
  transmute(
    sample    = sample_id,
    site      = if ("body_site" %in% names(metrics)) body_site else NA,
    group     = if ("group" %in% names(metrics)) group else NA,
    `input (M)`      = round(input_reads / 1e6, 1),
    `uniq %`         = round(unique_map_pct, 1),
    `multi %`        = round(multi_map_pct, 1),
    `too short %`    = round(unmapped_short_pct, 1),
    `rRNA %`         = round(rrna_pct, 1),
    `intergenic %`   = round(intergenic_pct, 1),
    `dup %`          = round(duplication_pct, 1),
    `assigned (M)`   = round(assigned_fragments / 1e6, 2),
    `genes 10+`      = genes_detected_10,
    `CV cov`         = round(median_cv_coverage, 2),
    `strand %`       = round(correct_strand_pct, 1)
  ) |>
  kable()
```

# Flags

```{r flag_logic}
flag_one <- function(value, direction, warn, fail) {
  if (is.na(value)) return("NA")
  if (!is.na(fail) && ((direction == "low" && value < fail) ||
                       (direction == "high" && value > fail))) return("FAIL")
  if (!is.na(warn) && ((direction == "low" && value < warn) ||
                       (direction == "high" && value > warn))) return("WARN")
  "PASS"
}

flags_long <- metrics |>
  select(sample_id, any_of(thresholds$metric)) |>
  pivot_longer(-sample_id, names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  left_join(thresholds, by = "metric") |>
  mutate(flag = pmap_chr(list(value, direction, warn, fail), flag_one))

flags_wide <- flags_long |>
  select(sample_id, label, flag) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = label, values_from = flag) |>
  left_join(select(metrics, sample_id, any_of(c("body_site", "group"))),
            by = "sample_id")
```

```{r verdicts}
value_of <- function(df, sample, metric) df[[metric]][df$sample_id == sample]

verdicts <- metrics |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    n_fail = sum(flags_long$flag[flags_long$sample_id == sample_id] == "FAIL"),
    n_warn = sum(flags_long$flag[flags_long$sample_id == sample_id] == "WARN"),
    locus_level_ok = !is.na(assigned_fragments) &&
      assigned_fragments >= locus_level_rules$assigned_fragments &&
      !is.na(genes_detected_10) &&
      genes_detected_10 >= locus_level_rules$genes_detected_10 &&
      (is.na(median_cv_coverage) ||
         median_cv_coverage <= locus_level_rules$median_cv_coverage),
    verdict = case_when(
      is_blank(if ("group" %in% names(metrics)) group else NA_character_) ~
        "blank control, not assessed",
      n_fail > 0 & !locus_level_ok ~ "review before use; ERV family level only",
      n_fail > 0                   ~ "review before use",
      !locus_level_ok              ~ "usable; ERV family level only",
      n_warn > 0                   ~ "usable, with warnings",
      TRUE                         ~ "usable"
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(sample_id, n_warn, n_fail, verdict)
```

```{r flag_table}
flags_wide |>
  left_join(verdicts, by = "sample_id") |>
  select(sample = sample_id, any_of(c("body_site", "group")),
         everything(), -n_warn, -n_fail) |>
  kable()
```

```{r thresholds_used}
thresholds |>
  transmute(Metric = label,
            Direction = if_else(direction == "low",
                                "low values flagged", "high values flagged"),
            Warn = warn, Fail = fail) |>
  kable(caption = "Thresholds in force for this report")
```

```{r write_out}
if (isTRUE(params$write_flags_tsv)) {
  out_file <- file.path(out_step, "qc_flags.tsv")
  metrics |>
    left_join(verdicts, by = "sample_id") |>
    write_tsv(out_file)
  cat("Flag table written to:", out_file, "\n")
}
```

# Samples needing attention

```{r attention}
attention <- flags_long |>
  filter(flag %in% c("WARN", "FAIL")) |>
  left_join(select(metrics, sample_id, any_of("group")), by = "sample_id") |>
  filter(!is_blank(if ("group" %in% names(metrics)) group else NA_character_)) |>
  transmute(sample = sample_id, metric = label, value = round(value, 2), flag) |>
  arrange(desc(flag), sample)

if (nrow(attention) == 0) {
  cat("No warnings raised.\n")
} else {
  kable(attention)
}
```

# Notes on interpretation

- Nothing here excludes a sample. Flags are warnings, and the decision to drop
  a sample stays with the analyst.
- The Picard ribosomal metric is not used for the rRNA flag. The 45S rDNA
  arrays are poorly represented in GRCh38, so Picard reports values near zero
  regardless of the true rRNA content. SortMeRNA carries this metric.
- The SortMeRNA eukaryotic database is a proxy for human rRNA: fungal rRNA also
  matches it, which may inflate the fraction at sites with fungal load.
- A high intergenic fraction can indicate residual genomic DNA, but it can also
  reflect unannotated transcription. Read it together with the correct-strand
  percentage: genomic DNA is unstranded, so a strand percentage near 50 would
  point to DNA carryover, while a high value argues against it.
- Locus-level ERV suitability uses depth, gene repertoire and coverage
  evenness. Family-level aggregation is the fallback primary readout, not a
  lesser analysis.
